Answer-only SAE features (issue #1482)

Descriptions are a reading aid, never evidence. This page carries answer-side evidence: described from the feature's own ANSWER-side activating windows (ans_max quantile bins), from #1773 full-dictionary release UNION the #1934 recovery. The #1773 standing caveat is that such descriptions are search-index-only — neighbour discrimination 0.322 against a 0.50 bar. This page is entirely descriptions, so that caveat carries more weight here than anywhere else, not less: any impression that these features form a recognisable kind comes from text that cannot reliably tell a feature from its neighbour.

"Never fires on the other side" is a strong criterion. It means zero across all 120,000 fit rows at ROW-OCCUPANCY grain — a feature counts as active if it fires anywhere in the span. A feature firing at a single token of a single answer is not answer-only. Membership is the 120,000-row census, NOT the 2,000-row per-token capture (whose one-sided sets are several times larger purely because fewer rows give a feature fewer chances to fire on the other side).

What is shown. All 2,164 features that fire somewhere in the ANSWER span and NEVER in the context, ranked by answer-side firing frequency (activity) descending. 2,152 of 2,164 carry a answer-side evidence description (12 without one); 788 of 2,164 have a scored R².

Sort key. the activity column of the full-width covariates — rows in which the feature fires anywhere in the ANSWER span, divided by 120,000.

R² is the full-width dense-context → SAE-answer ridge read (121,111 of 131,072 dictionary columns are scored; the rest have zero holdout answer variance). Unscored is shown as unscored, never as R² = 0.

Companion artifacts. The per-token answer-side ratio panel figures/issue_1482/side_specificity/side_ratio_token.png uses this same census membership (1,654 / 2,164 as its two point masses). The sibling page is context-only sae features — note it carries context-side evidence descriptions, a DIFFERENT instrument from this page's answer-side evidence ones. The two description sets share a describer prompt and judge but draw their windows from opposite spans, so they must not be pooled or compared as one set; each row on each page is badged with its evidence side.
